title: Chained USB printing, with safe Stop
lede: The helper prints batches with one initial blank and no blank strips between labels. Stop and remaining-only recovery preserve exact copy history.

stats.n: Blank strips: accepted independent output versus accepted chained output
All six layouts and four production QR scans accepted

sections.heading: Same approved layout, clearer printer behavior
sections.note: Matched 1440 × 1100 browser fixture, same single label, empty history, role and scroll. The approved preview bytes are identical. Native JPEG originals are retained beside lossless PNG conversions.

pairs.afterCap: SDK chaining, expected tape costs and retained print history.

sections.heading: Actual Stop and remaining-only recovery
sections.note: After-only hardware evidence: active job metadata and USB pixels were physically checked by the user. This fixture proves integration with real USB; its Dev Staff name is not a production-authenticated identity.

shots.cap: Stop landed during B. A/B completed, C remained unsent. User confirmed A/B only plus two blanks.
After reload and an explicit Continue, the linked child contained only C. User confirmed C once, no duplicate A/B.

sections.heading: Failure recovery
sections.note: After-only, simulated USB through the real helper. No physical output in this failure scenario.

shots.cap: A failed local completion save stays visible after passive refresh. Saving that exact pending log emitted no print/feed commands.

changes.was: An independent label could be settled after its own completion. Chaining can leave the last label held inside the printer.
changes.now: Every intermediate page stays provisional until the final feed succeeds. Failures retain all affected copy identities for separate physical review.

changes.h: Stop has an explicit finish intent
changes.was: An interrupted chain could leave a held label and no confirmed release.
changes.now: Stop sends no further label content. It first saves a finish intent, then sends only the verified zero-ink release. Close, error and reload never feed or retry.

changes.was: A generic repeated sample made duplicate counts hard to verify.
changes.now: Fresh A/B/C tests and linked child receipts proved remaining-only output. A/B were excluded when C was continued. Downloadable receipts retain operator, text/QR, timestamps and copy identity.

verification: All five production-encoder packets matched the offline SDK reference bytes; the Stop feed is exactly 59 bytes with the pinned accepted hash.
109 focused tests and 11 real disposable PostgreSQL service/audit/lineage cases passed.
TypeScript, touched-file ESLint, migration-free app build, codemaps/docs and whitespace checks passed.
Independent safety review: no remaining P1/P2 after fixing passive refresh discarding an in-memory pending completion.
Fresh browser page has no console errors; phone-width smoke and tablet dialog/Escape/focus return passed.
notes: One initial blank per normal batch remains. Stopping early adds a small blank to release the held tail; the A/B Stop test produced two blanks in total.
The earlier unlettered recovery count stays unverified because the user forgot it. Its raw receipt was retained; those copies were not replayed.
The Brother app was closed. No macOS security settings changed and live debugger capture was abandoned after macOS denied attachment.
No application migration, commit, push or deployment. Authenticated managed-preview proof, application of prepared migration 0198, physical mid-transfer cable pull and tape-out remain separate gates.
